solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Return of hooter ahead of work's end causes criticism

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for a nose is read from its end

parts.note: hooter and conk are both slang for the nose

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of work

explanation.surface: An owl hooting before the working day is over draws complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for a nose, as is conk; 'ahead of' just places the turned word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock is informal for adverse comment or a piece of disparagement, as in taking a knock in the press.

clue.text: Is section in sailing boat to go west

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the boat

parts.note: a koff is a Dutch two-masted sailing vessel
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A part of a yacht heads westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west' is slang for die, not a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiss off is slang for to die, the same euphemism as going west.

clue.text: Checked over a custom zip

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end

parts.note: sat on means held in check, suppressed
taken as written
usage is established custom

explanation.surface: Inspecting a customary zipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a sausage' is British slang for nothing at all, and zip is US slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying nothing whatsoever, a colloquial synonym for zero.

clue.text: Commoner once caught by Anglo-Saxon noble

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the Old English word for a nobleman

explanation.surface: An ordinary man in history is captured by a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceorl was a freeman of the lowest rank in Anglo-Saxon England, a historical commoner.

clue.text: Dancing turned dark on whistle

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, read backwards

parts.note: murk is darkness
a ping is a high whistling sound, like a bullet

explanation.surface: Dancers spin in the dark to a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Krumping is an energetic street dance style that began in Los Angeles.

clue.text: Win account with energy in place of great industry

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account

indicators.note: in tells us the energy letter sits inside the word for a busy place

parts.note: a beehive is proverbially a scene of tireless work
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A firm wins a contract while swapping heavy industry for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as substitution, but it is just 'in' a place: the energy letter goes into the hive, and nothing is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something and to achieve it both mean to gain it by effort, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Ace snatched up being of face value

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: rapt in its old sense means seized or carried off

explanation.surface: A top card grabbed and shown for what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A share at par trades at its nominal or face value, neither above nor below it.

clue.text: Fruit from old hedge stuffed into shelter

indicators.note: stuffed into puts one word inside another

parts.note: a cote is a small shelter for birds or animals
hay is an obsolete word for a hedge

explanation.surface: Produce from an ancient hedgerow crammed into a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The chayote is a pear-shaped green fruit of a climbing gourd plant, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bones trouble one getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means rising, so read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Aching joints bother someone rising from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilia is the plural of ilium, the broad upper bone of the pelvis.

clue.text: What grows in the main? Largesse surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement of these letters

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asking what flourishes mostly, and answering with generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, not 'mainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelgrass is a flowering marine plant that grows underwater in shallow seas.

clue.text: With it this gas could show the extent of your endurance say

parts.note: at the end of your tether means you can endure no more
't is an old contracted form of it, as in 'tis

explanation.surface: Adding something would show how far your patience stretches.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'T in front and the gas becomes the limit of endurance; so the answer is that limit without 'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a volatile gas or vapour formerly used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Conspicuous chap pushed off on the other side once

parts.note: overt means openly visible
a chap is a he
to push off is to leave, so pushed off means went away

explanation.surface: A showy man shoved away to the far side long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Over the left (shoulder) is old slang tacked on to say the opposite of what was just said, so it fits 'on the other side' as a contrary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase signalled that the speaker meant the contrary, taking the other side of a statement in an obsolete idiom.

clue.text: Buccaneering bold Boer holding up to end in Kimberley

parts.note: free can mean forward or bold

indicators.note: holding means having something inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Kimberley

explanation.surface: A daring Boer raids his way to Kimberley.
explanation.walkthrough: Kimberley is a South African diamond town, fitting the Boer surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebootery is the practice of piracy or plundering, which is what buccaneering means.

clue.text: A pot runs freely for Rab C's cuppa

indicators.note: running freely means moving without set order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A teapot pours easily when a Glaswegian wants his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C. Nesbitt is a Glaswegian TV comedy character, so his cuppa is a Scots word for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroupan is a Scots dialect term for a pot of tea, the drink a Glasgow man would call his cuppa.

clue.text: Scots serve relish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Scots verb meaning to serve
second meaning: in Scots, to savour

explanation.surface: Scottish people dish up chutney.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are Scots words, so 'Scots' governs the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the same word means both to serve someone and to savour or taste something.

clue.text: Bait full of English grain

indicators.note: a word that is full of something holds it inside

parts.note: in British slang to be in a bait is to be in a temper
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Fishing bait stuffed with English corn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bait looks like the angler's lure; here it is the informal British word for a fit of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragee, or ragi, is a millet cereal grown in India and Africa as a staple crop.

clue.text: Overcome by cursing ways to avoid clobber

parts.note: an out is an escape route
clobber is British slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Swearing is beaten by ways of dodging a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like the verb to hit; here it is slang for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outswear someone is to beat them at swearing, to overcome them with oaths.

clue.text: Professional who salts old mackerel

parts.note: pro is short for professional
one who cures meat or fish with salt

explanation.surface: An expert fishmonger salting a mackerel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mackerel is an archaic word for a pimp, not the fish, despite the salting.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurer is a pimp, which is what mackerel meant in old slang borrowed from French maquereau.

clue.text: Heart trouble or perhaps an affliction of eccentricity?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inflammation of the heart
second meaning: read as being a card (an eccentric) plus the suffix for a disease

explanation.surface: A medical query whether a cardiac complaint is really just oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an eccentric person, and -itis is a suffix for a disease, so the playful second reading invents an illness of oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: Carditis is the medical term for inflammation of the heart muscle or its lining.

clue.text: Female is accepted by one to advise person up on animals

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: an agony aunt gives advice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman gets taken on by a counsellor for someone keen on wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: An agony aunt writes a newspaper advice column, hence one to advise.
explanation.definitionFit: A faunist is a naturalist who studies the animal life of a region, so is well informed about animals.

clue.text: People who polish ornamental wood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those who smooth surfaces with sandpaper
second meaning: red sandalwood used for decoration

explanation.surface: Workers buffing decorative timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanders smooth a surface with abrasives, and sanders is also a name for red sandalwood timber.

clue.text: Particularly graceful horse leading a carriage

parts.note: the Arab is a breed of horse noted for elegance
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elegant horse pulls a coach at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An araba is a heavy wheeled cart or coach used in Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: New cola recipe with slices of zest added the icing for Spaniards

indicators.note: making something new means rearranging it

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

indicators.note: a slice off the start of each word takes its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A fresh cola mix with bits of citrus peel tossed in, topping off a Spanish cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcorza is a Spanish sugar paste or icing used to coat sweets and cakes.

clue.text: Play around beside mattress

indicators.note: around says one word wraps about the other

parts.note: play and fun are both amusement
to can mean against or beside, as in cheek to cheek

explanation.surface: Children romp about next to a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress laid on the floor or on a frame.

clue.text: Busy loos are getting a spray

indicators.note: busy things bustle about, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Crowded toilets are given a squirt of air freshener.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can whose contents come out as a fine spray of droplets.

clue.text: Determined aged sins in a new way

indicators.note: doing something in a new way means arranging it differently

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone resolutely commits old sins afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determined' looks like an adjective for resolve; it is the past participle meaning fixed or allotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing determined, in the sense of fixed or allotted, has been assigned to someone.

clue.text: Suffering conversion beast makes good

indicators.note: something that undergoes a conversion is changed into a different form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A monster undergoes a change of heart and reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to back or support, helping another along, so it serves for making something good.

clue.text: Study that's held back by primary assembly

indicators.note: back means read from right to left
held means contained within the words that follow

parts.note: letters inside these words, read backwards

explanation.surface: Schoolwork kept in after morning assembly at a primary school.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a written study or composition on a particular subject.

clue.text: Copper nabbing Oscar, hollow rotten process which stands out

indicators.note: nabbing means seizing and holding inside

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Oscar is O in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: hollowed out leaves only the outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of rotten

explanation.surface: A policeman arrests Oscar in a corrupt, empty proceeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Process is the anatomical sense, a projecting part of a bone, not a procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornu is a horn-shaped projection in anatomy, the sort of process that sticks out from a bone.

clue.text: Raunchy ode that's been cut short in past

indicators.note: in places the shortened poem inside the word for past

parts.note: gone by means past

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its tail, dropping a final letter

parts.note: an awdl is a Welsh ode in strict metre

explanation.surface: A lewd poem that was trimmed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: An awdl is a strict-metre Welsh ode, a word mostly met in Mephisto-level vocabulary; 'past' is gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawdy and raunchy both describe humour or writing that is coarse and sexually frank.

clue.text: Heartlessly put out something unpleasant

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly snuffs out a nasty thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose of something, like a dose of flu, is a portion of an unpleasant experience.

clue.text: Aware of directly avoiding present

indicators.note: a word avoiding something leaves it out

parts.note: pronto means at once
pr is a dictionary abbreviation for present, as in the tense

explanation.surface: Knowing about something straight away while dodging a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: PR as present is a grammar abbreviation (pr. p. for present participle), so it drops from PRONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be onto someone is idiomatic for being aware of what they are up to.

clue.text: Bureau finally sacked one who tests old charger

indicators.note: the final letter is sacked, that is dismissed from the word

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk
one who tries something out

explanation.surface: An office chief is fired by an examiner over an outdated charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A destrier was a medieval knight's warhorse, and charger is the old word for such a mount.

clue.text: Conundrum about series that was out in the mid-afternoon?

definitions.text: that was out in the mid-afternoon?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle
a train of events is a series

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a run of things that went missing mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the utensil comes out at teatime, around four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer is set out at teatime in the afternoon to catch leaves when pouring from the pot.

clue.text: Shed's front with loads of locks gets you uptight

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of shed
having plenty of tresses, or locks of hair

explanation.surface: A shed door with many padlocks makes you anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks look like door fastenings but are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressy is informal for anxious or tense, the same state as being uptight.

clue.text: French on, oh, returning deity

parts.note: sur is French for on

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old exclamation of surprise, like oh

explanation.surface: A Frenchman exclaims at a god coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Surya is the Hindu sun god, a deity of the Vedic pantheon.
